issues.problem: Round-1 fixes to commands[0] and commands[2] are in. But a child alone at the screen has no teacher in the room, and from the tutor avatar 'Clap for your teacher' means 'clap for me', which sounds odd. It also does not use the teacher card.
The chant brings in a new name, Sam, who is not in the story (Tom and Anna). The child says 'I am Sam', which can confuse a beginner.

Round-1 fix is only partly done. 'Write the word cat.' is spelling from listening (PREA1-07), not copying: no card or line shows the word cat to copy, so PREA1-10 is still not practised. 'copy' is not a Starters word, so the command cannot say it either.
Round-1 issues are fixed (the clap command is gone and outcomeIds is fixed). But the lesson word 'number' is not in the story.
issues.suggestion: They count to ten. Ten is a big number!

issues.problem: Ben has only one book, so 'Count the books.' has nothing to count. The apples (four) work better.

The round-1 fix is still confusing. 'Sam counts his balls. Sixteen, seventeen...' makes counting seem to start at sixteen, the same problem round 1 found in story[3]. Sam also appears without being introduced.
issues.suggestion: Sam counts his balls. There are twenty balls!

issues.problem: 'count them' is unclear: count what? The fish, the balls or the birds?
issues.suggestion: Lucy and Sam can count to twenty. Hooray!

issues.problem: PREA1-02 (respond to simple questions) is still weak. The questions in the chant have no answers, so the child never practises answering 'How many?'.
Round-1 fix is in. But a child alone at a screen or desk has no picture of a sun to colour. Nothing gives them one, so they cannot do it.
Round-1 fixes are in. But drawing a whole family (up to seven people) takes too long in a listen-and-do lesson. It can also upset a child who has lost a parent.
Round-1 fixes are in. But the lesson words 'head' and 'body' are still not in the story.
issues.suggestion: He can put his hands on his head. Tom is happy.

issues.problem: 'Smile.' does not practise any lesson word. 'feet' is not practised in the commands either.
Round-1 fix is only partly done. 'skirt' is now in the chant but is still not in the story, so 'Look at the skirt.' still comes from nowhere.
issues.suggestion: It is a nice day. Mum has a long skirt.

issues.problem: In Gulf and Arab homes children take off their shoes indoors. A child at the screen at home will often have no shoes on to show.
A child alone at a screen or desk has no picture of a jacket to colour.

Round-1 fixes are in. But the order is wrong: 'Close your book.' (commands[5]) comes before the book is ever opened. A child at home may also have no school bag at the desk and would have to leave the screen to open it.
With the change above, 'bag' is no longer practised. The desk is already practised in commands[6].
